```{r}
base_model <- aov(Ameisen ~ Brot + Belag + Butter, data = Sandwich)

lm_base_model <- lm(Ameisen ~ Brot + Belag + Butter, data = Sandwich)

assumption_check_bm <- data.frame(res = resid(base_model), fit = fitted(base_model))


ggplot(assumption_check_bm, aes(x = fit, y = res)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = paste("Residuen vs. vorhergesagte Werte |","SSE:",round(sum(assumption_check_bm$res^2))),
    x = "Vorhergesagte Werte",
    y = "Residuen"
  )

qq_plot <- ggplot(assumption_check_bm, aes(sample = res)) +
  stat_qq(aes(color = "Residuen")) +             # Punkte: Residuen
  stat_qq_line(aes(color = "Theoretische Normalverteilung"), linewidth = 0.8) +  # Linie mit Label
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,                            # Titel der Legende
    values = c(
      "Residuen" = "black",
      "Theoretische Normalverteilung" = "red"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(hjust = 1),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    plot.background = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "bottom"                   # Legende unterhalb des Plots
  ) +
labs(
  title = "Q-Q-Plot der Residuen",
  x = "Theoretische Quantile der Normalverteilung",
  y = "Empirische Quantile der Residuen"
)


ggsave("qq_plot.png", plot = qq_plot, dpi = 600, width = 5.99, height = 4.05, units = "in", bg = "white")
```

```{r}
lm_base_model <- lm(Ameisen ~ Brot + Belag + Butter, data = Sandwich)

# Koeffizienten und Standardfehler
coefs <- coef(lm_base_model)
ses   <- sqrt(diag(vcov(lm_base_model)))

# Tabellieren (nur Base R)
tab <- data.frame(
  term = names(coefs),
  estimate = as.numeric(coefs),
  se = as.numeric(ses),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 95%-Konfidenzintervalle
tab$lower <- tab$estimate - 1.96 * tab$se
tab$upper <- tab$estimate + 1.96 * tab$se

# Interzept raus
tab <- tab[tab$term != "(Intercept)", ]

# Hilfsfunktion: Faktorname + Stufe aus dem Term extrahieren
# (angenommen: Kontraste sind die Standards -> Namen wie "BrotMehrkorn", "BelagErdnussbutter", "Butternein")
split_factor_level <- function(x) {
  # Welche der drei Faktoren steckt drin?
  if (startsWith(x, "Brot"))  return(c("Brot",  sub("^Brot",  "", x)))
  if (startsWith(x, "Belag")) return(c("Belag", sub("^Belag", "", x)))
  if (startsWith(x, "Butter"))return(c("Butter",sub("^Butter","", x)))
  return(c(NA_character_, x))
}

tmp <- t(vapply(tab$term, split_factor_level, FUN.VALUE = character(2)))
tab$Faktor <- tmp[,1]
tab$Stufe  <- tmp[,2]

# Nur die drei gewünschten Faktoren behalten (falls im Modell mehr steckt)
tab <- tab[tab$Faktor %in% c("Brot","Belag","Butter"), ]

# Für hübsche Achsenbeschriftung
tab$Faktor <- factor(tab$Faktor, levels = c("Brot","Belag","Butter"))


ggplot(tab, aes(x = estimate, y = Stufe)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_grid(Faktor ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Effektschätzer (Differenz zur Referenz) mit 95%-Konfidenzintervallen",
    x = "Schätzer (β)",
    y = "Stufe"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
lm_base_model <- lm(Ameisen ~ Brot + Belag + Butter, data = Sandwich)

# ---------- Hilfsfunktionen ----------

# partielle eta^2 je Faktor aus einer ANOVA-Tabelle berechnen
eta_p2_from_anova <- function(lm_fit) {
  tab <- anova(lm_fit)                 # DataFrame: Rownames = Faktoren, letzte Zeile = Residuals
  ss_err <- tab["Residuals", "Sum Sq"] # Fehler-SS
  fac_rows <- setdiff(rownames(tab), "Residuals")
  eta <- sapply(fac_rows, function(f)
    tab[f, "Sum Sq"] / (tab[f, "Sum Sq"] + ss_err)
  )
  data.frame(Faktor = fac_rows, eta_p2 = as.numeric(eta), row.names = NULL)
}

# Bootstrap-CIs für partielle eta^2 je Faktor (nur Base R)
eta_p2_boot <- function(formula, data, B = 1000, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  n <- nrow(data)
  # Namen der Faktoren aus Originalfit
  lm0 <- lm(formula, data = data)
  fac_names <- eta_p2_from_anova(lm0)$Faktor
  mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = B, ncol = length(fac_names))
  colnames(mat) <- fac_names
  for (b in 1:B) {
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)  # Resampling der Zeilen
    fitb <- lm(formula, data = data[idx, , drop = FALSE])
    eb <- eta_p2_from_anova(fitb)
    # auf gemeinsame Reihenfolge mappen
    mat[b, ] <- eb$eta_p2[match(fac_names, eb$Faktor)]
  }
  # Perzentil-CIs
  ci <- t(apply(mat, 2, function(x) quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)))
  data.frame(Faktor = fac_names,
             lower = ci[,1],
             upper = ci[,2],
             row.names = NULL)
}

# ---------- Schätzung + CIs berechnen ----------

eta_point <- eta_p2_from_anova(lm_base_model)                    # Punktschätzer
eta_ci    <- eta_p2_boot(Ameisen ~ Brot + Belag + Butter,
                         data = Sandwich, B = 2000, seed = 42)   # 95%-CI via Bootstrap

plot_df <- merge(eta_point, eta_ci, by = "Faktor")

# Faktor-Reihenfolge (optional hübsch)
plot_df$Faktor <- factor(plot_df$Faktor, levels = c("Brot", "Belag", "Butter"))

# ---------- Plot (ggplot2) ----------

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Faktor, y = eta_p2)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Faktoreffekte (partielles Eta-Quadrat) mit 95%-Konfidenzintervallen",
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(partielles~eta^2)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

```{r}
base_model <- aov(Ameisen ~ Brot + Belag + Butter, data = Sandwich)

# Tukey-Paarvergleiche
tk <- TukeyHSD(base_model)

# In einen Data Frame verwandeln (für alle Faktoren)
df_list <- lapply(names(tk), function(f){
  d <- as.data.frame(tk[[f]])
  d$contrast <- rownames(d)
  d$factor   <- f
  rownames(d) <- NULL
  # Spaltennamen säubern (p adj -> p_adj)
  names(d) <- sub("^p adj$", "p_adj", names(d))
  d
})
tk_df <- do.call(rbind, df_list)

# Optional: Signifikanzflag (für Farbe)
tk_df$sig <- tk_df$p_adj < 0.05

# Kontraste je Faktor sortieren (optisch schöner)
# -> Reihenfolge nach Effektgröße (|diff|) pro Faktor
tk_df$contrast <- with(tk_df, reorder(contrast, abs(diff)))

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(tk_df, aes(x = diff, y = contrast, color = sig)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.7, linetype = 2) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr), height = 0) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey30", "TRUE" = "black"),
                     breaks = c(TRUE, FALSE),
                     labels = c("p < 0.05", "n. s."),
                     name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = "Tukey-Paarvergleiche: Schätzer und 95%-Konfidenzintervalle",
    x = "Differenz der Mittelwerte (Kontrast)",
    y = "Paarvergleich"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8)
  )


tk_df$label <- with(tk_df, paste(factor, contrast, sep = ": "))
# Für eine sinnvolle Reihenfolge nach absoluter Effektgröße
tk_df$label <- with(tk_df, reorder(label, abs(diff)))

library(ggplot2)

tk_df$contrast <- c("M.Korn-Weiß","V.Korn-Weiß","Roggen-Weiß","V.Korn-M.Korn","Roggen-M.Korn","Roggen-V.Korn","E.Butter-Gurke Schinken","Hefe-Gurke Schinken","Hefe-E.Butter","Butter-o.Butter")

              geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.7, linetype = 2) +
              geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr), height = 0) +
              geom_point(size = 2.5) +
              scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "Blue", "TRUE" = "black"),
                     breaks = c(TRUE, FALSE),
                     labels = c("p < 0.05", "n. s."),
                     name = NULL) +
              labs(
              title = "Tukey-Paarvergleiche",
              subtitle = "Schätzer und 95%-Konfidenzintervalle",
              x = "Differenz der Mittelwerte (Kontrast)",

              ) +

              theme(
              legend.position = "top",

              panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
              plot.background = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3)
              )

# Falls die Spalte wirklich "factor" heißt, besser umbenennen, um Verwirrung zu vermeiden:
```

```{r}
# Pakete
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)

# ======= PARAMETER =======
# Hier den Faktor wählen: "Brot", "Belag" oder "Butter"
fac <- "Belag"     # <- nach Bedarf ändern
width_right <- 0.8 # Breite der kleinen Dichteformen
width_left  <- 1.6 # Breite der großen Gesamtdichte links

# ======= DATENFRAME =======
# Falls dein Frame anders heißt, hier ersetzen:
df <- Sandwich

# ======= GESAMTDICHTE (links) =======
d_all <- density(df$Ameisen)
all_df <- tibble(y = d_all$x, dens = d_all$y)

# Polygon für die linke (gedrehte) Gesamtdichte schließen
poly_all <- bind_rows(
  all_df |> transmute(x = -dens * width_left, y),
  all_df |> arrange(desc(y)) |> transmute(x = 0, y)
) |> mutate(group = "ALL")

# ======= BEDINGTE DICHTEN je Faktorstufe =======
levs <- levels(df[[fac]])
# Dichten
dens_list <- map_dfr(levs, function(lv){
  d <- density(df$Ameisen[df[[fac]] == lv])
  tibble(level = lv, y = d$x, dens = d$y)
})

# Skaliere auf eine einheitliche Breite nach rechts
max_dens <- max(dens_list$dens)
dens_list <- dens_list |>
  mutate(pos = as.numeric(factor(level, levels = levs)),
         xcurve = pos + (dens / max_dens) * width_right)

# Baue geschlossene Polygone (Kurve + Baseline am pos)
poly_groups <- dens_list |>
  group_by(level, pos) |>
  arrange(y, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    x = list(c(xcurve, rev(rep(first(pos), n())))),
    y = list(c(y, rev(y))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  unnest(c(x, y))

# ======= MITTELWERTE & SD je Stufe =======
summ <- df |>
  group_by(level = .data[[fac]]) |>
  summarise(mu = mean(Ameisen), sd = sd(Ameisen), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pos = as.numeric(factor(level, levels = levs)))

# ======= PLOT =======
ggplot() +
  # Linke Gesamtdichte
  geom_polygon(data = poly_all,
               aes(x = x, y = y),
               fill = "orange", alpha = 0.75, color = NA) +

  # Vertikale Hilfslinien pro Stufe
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq_along(levs), linetype = 3, linewidth = 0.3) +

  # Bedingte Dichtepolygone (rechts)
  geom_polygon(data = poly_groups,
               aes(x = x, y = y, group = level, fill = level),
               alpha = 0.9, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +

  # Mittelwerte (Punkte) und SD als vertikale Segmente
  geom_segment(data = summ,
               aes(x = pos, xend = pos, y = pmax(mu - sd, min(df$Ameisen)),
                   yend = pmin(mu + sd, max(df$Ameisen))),
               linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = summ, aes(x = pos, y = mu),
             size = 2, color = "black") +

  # Achsen & Labels
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(levs),
    labels = levs,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.05)) # Platz links für die große Dichte
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues") +
  labs(
    x = fac, y = "Ameisen",
    title = "ANOVA-Illustration: Gesamtdichte und Y|X-Dichten",
    subtitle = paste0("X = ", fac, "  •  Punkte = Mittelwerte, Segmente = ±1 SD")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

```
